correctness.rationale: Incident edges are always compatible in the bipartite graph. Disjoint edges are compatible precisely when their two cross edges are missing, which makes them a unique reciprocal pair. A third compatible edge would have to intersect both, hence be one of the missing cross edges. All other packings of size at least two are subsets of a star with unique center, and minimum degree two rules out empty or singleton maximal packings. This proves both polynomials and the exact extrema on substituting p=q. Inclusion-maximal sizes first differ at one deletion; it takes two deletions for the minimum to drop to two when n>=4. An independent definition-level compatibility search matched both polynomials in all 78 triples with 3<=p,q<=6 (15,961 sets). For (4,4,2) the coefficient lists from degree zero are [1,14,37,20,4] and [0,0,1,4,4].
residual_risks: Finite computation is a regression check only; the argument gives all sizes.
